title: Don't scale barely profitable ads
transcript: Whatever numbers you're seeing in the very beginning when you first start running those ads at a couple hundred dollars a day and spend, those will never be the numbers that you're getting when you're at two, three, 4, five, $10,000 in spend. It almost always gets worse as you scale. Your cost per click is going to go up. Your cost per thousand impressions is going to go up. Maybe your click through rates gonna go down as Facebook shows it to a colder and colder audience. Uh, your opt in rates gonna lower, your booking rates gonna lower. People have seen the message multiple time. The ad fatigues, one of a million different things is gonna cause, uh, your advertising campaigns to be worse than when you first started. So that's another really great lesson is when you're first running the campaigns and you get your first sale, but you're barely break even on the advertising campaign, don't run out there and try to start scaling it immediately because you want to make sure that you are hilariously profitable in the very beginning so that when you scale and ultimately those numbers start working against you, you still have, let's say, a 30% margin of error across the entire board.
